        Home Inventory User Manual

        Home Inventory User Manual

        For Home Inventory v2.95

        Home Inventory keeps a record of the things you own: what they are, where they are, what they're worth, and the photos, receipts and warranties that prove it. This manual starts with the most important setup step, choosing where your data file lives.

        1. A tour of the app: what each area is for

        Home Inventory started as a list of what you own, but it now does much more. People use it for home insurance records, moving, a rental property, a collection, office equipment, a car's service history, or a family's travel and shopping lists. This chapter describes each area in a few lines so you can pick the parts that fit how you use it. The ☰ button at the top left lists every function in one place, with a Find a function box.

        Welcome screen

        When the app opens it asks What would you like to do today? and shows the main areas as large buttons: add, snap, find, scan, browse, reports, checklists, vehicles, moving, backups, settings and help. Tap one to go straight there, or Go to my inventory. Turn it off with the box at the bottom, or in Settings › When the app opens; open it any time from the ☰ menu.

        Home screen and dashboard

        The top shows Summary (number of items, total and average value, rooms), then Rooms, Categories and Types. Tap any box to show just those items. Each panel folds with its arrow; Settings › When the app opens chooses whether panels start folded or stay the way you left them.

        Items

        Add Item records a name, category, room and spot, type, value, serial number, photo, receipt, warranty, tags and notes. Snap & Add starts from a photo. Tap an item to see everything about it; Edit changes it. Star an item to make it a favorite, or tap Move to mark it for a move.

        Finding things

        Type in Search and tap Go (searching with nothing typed shows everything). Sort orders or groups the list, Filter narrows it by category, room, spot, type or tag, and View switches between Cards, List and Lines. All clears everything and shows every item.

        Scan

        Reads the QR labels the app prints and product barcodes (UPC, EAN). A known item opens right away; a new barcode lets you add it, with AI suggestions inside the Claude app.

        Reports

        Printable reports for insurance, items by room, by category and by type, personal property tax, maintenance due, vehicle maintenance and a one-line list of everything. Missing Items, Stolen Items and the Police Report appear only when something is marked that way. Every report can be filtered, printed or saved as a PDF, and emailed with the Email button beside Print. Inside the Claude app, which can't open a print window, Print / Save PDF saves a PDF to your device instead; open it to print, share or attach it. Print and Email just above the item list (and Current View in the Reports menu) turns exactly what the list is showing, with your search, filters, sort and groups, into a page to print or email.

        Vehicles and maintenance

        Give an item the type Vehicle to track mileage, VIN, plate, service reminders by miles or months, and a service history with receipts. Any item can also have a maintenance task that repeats, such as a furnace filter.

        Documents

        Give an item the type Document to keep a scan or PDF of a policy, deed or passport, where the paper copy is kept, and when it renews.

        Moving and labels

        Packing List checks items into numbered boxes and prints box lists. Print Labels prints QR labels for items or boxes; scan a label to open the item.

        Checklists

        Travel Packing and Household Supplies are check-off lists. Under A check means, choose whether a check marks what's done (packed, or in stock) or what's still needed (to pack, or to buy), whichever fits how you work. Print makes a printable page (and every report has an Email button next to Print: send the report as text in an email, copy it, or save it as a file or PDF to attach): every item with empty boxes to fill in by hand, every item as checked now, or only what's still needed, such as a shopping list. Find them under Reports › Checklists or in the ☰ menu. Tap Add common items to start with the usual toiletries, clothing and travel essentials, or the household supplies most homes restock. Add your own, remove what you don't need, and tap Reset all to uncheck everything for next time. While you're looking at Consumable items, a button opens the Household Supplies list.

        Data and files

        The Data menu holds the Inventory File (one file in iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox), backups, Excel and CSV export and import, Combine Files to merge old backups without duplicates, and the Import templates (in Settings).

        Sharing and Household Sync

        Household Sync keeps one shared copy online for every device and family member. Share the App emails a copy of the app, with or without your items.

        More than one inventory

        The inventory menu at the top keeps separate inventories, for example a home, a cabin, an office or a collection. Sample Home is a ready-made example to practice on.

        Settings

        Choose the accent color, light or dark, which panels show, Backgrounds for the panels (one for all, or one per panel, including your own photo), whether dollar values show on screen, and how the app opens.

        Ideas for different uses

        • Insurance: photos, receipts and serial numbers, then the Insurance Report. Mark high-value pieces with a tag such as appraised.
        • Moving: mark items to move, pack them into boxes with the Packing List, and print box labels.
        • Rental or vacation property: one inventory per property, with maintenance tasks and the Items by Room report for check-ins.
        • Collections: a separate inventory with tags for series or condition, photos, and the Summary report.
        • Small office: type Equipment, serial numbers, warranty dates and the tax report.
        • Family life: the travel and household checklists, shared with Household Sync.

        2. Set up your data file (iCloud, OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox)

        Data › Inventory File first asks Where do you keep your files?: iCloud Drive, OneDrive / Microsoft 365, Google Drive, Dropbox, or just this device. Pick yours and the window shows the steps for that service, including how to keep the file synced and available offline. The steps below use OneDrive as the example; the other services work the same way with their own folder.

        The app always saves your items in your web browser. On top of that, you can keep everything in one file called inventory.json. Put that file in OneDrive and you can open the same inventory on your computer, phone or tablet, and it is backed up in the cloud.

        Where you use the appWhat happens
        Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a Windows PC or MacThe app links to the file and saves every change to it automatically. Recommended.
        Safari or Firefox on a computerYou open the file, and use Save now after making changes. The new copy goes to Downloads, and you move it into OneDrive.
        iPhone, iPad or AndroidYou open the file from OneDrive, and use Save now to save it back through the share menu.

        Before you start

        • Computer: install the OneDrive app and sign in. Windows 10 and 11 usually have it already. On a Mac, get it from the App Store. A OneDrive folder then appears in your file windows.
        • Phone or tablet: install the OneDrive app and sign in. On iPhone, also turn on OneDrive in the Files app: Files › Browse › ••• › Edit, then switch on OneDrive.
        • Save the Home Inventory app file (the .html file) somewhere you can find it, then open it in Chrome or Edge.

        Windows (Chrome or Edge)

        1. Open Home Inventory and click Data › Inventory File.
        2. Click Create inventory.json.
        3. In the save window, click OneDrive in the left sidebar. Open a folder such as Documents, or make a new folder called Home Inventory.
        4. Keep the name inventory.json and click Save.
        5. If the browser asks to let the site edit files, click Edit files or Allow.

        The footer now shows inventory.json · saved today at … · auto-save on. That's it. Every change is saved to OneDrive about a second later.

        Mac (Chrome or Edge)

        1. Click Data › Inventory File › Create inventory.json.
        2. In the save window, click the arrow next to the file name to show the full window if needed. Pick OneDrive under Locations in the sidebar, then a folder.
        3. Click Save, and allow the app to edit the file if asked.
        On a Mac, Safari can't link to the file. Use Chrome or Edge for automatic saving, or follow the Safari steps below.

        Safari or Firefox on a computer

        1. Click Data › Inventory File › Create inventory.json. The file is saved to your Downloads folder.
        2. Move inventory.json from Downloads into your OneDrive folder.
        3. Next time, start with Open existing file and pick inventory.json from OneDrive.
        4. After making changes, click Save now (the footer and an orange dot on Data remind you), then move the new copy into OneDrive and replace the old one.

        iPhone or iPad

        1. Open the Home Inventory app file in Safari (for example, from OneDrive or an email attachment).
        2. To start a new file: tap Data › Inventory File › Create inventory.json. In the share menu, tap Save to Files, pick OneDrive, choose a folder, and tap Save.
        3. To use a file you already have: tap Open existing file, tap Browse, pick OneDrive and choose inventory.json, then tap Load file.
        4. After making changes, tap Save now › Save to Files › OneDrive, pick the same folder, and tap Replace when asked.

        Android

        1. Open the app file in Chrome.
        2. Tap Data › Inventory File › Create inventory.json. In the share menu, pick OneDrive (or Save to Drive/Files), choose a folder, and save.
        3. On later visits, tap Open existing file and pick inventory.json from OneDrive (in the file picker, open the menu and choose OneDrive).
        4. After making changes, tap Save now and save it back to the same OneDrive folder.

        Saving somewhere other than OneDrive

        You don't have to use OneDrive. In the save window you can pick any folder on your computer, such as Documents, or another cloud folder like Google Drive, Dropbox or iCloud Drive. Everything in this manual works the same way.

        Using the same file on a second device

        1. Open the app on the other device and click Data › Inventory File › Open existing file.
        2. Pick inventory.json from your OneDrive folder.
        3. Check the message (it shows how many items the file has) and click Load file. This replaces whatever was in the app on that device.
        Use one device at a time. If you edit on your PC and phone at the same time, the app can't merge the changes. It will ask which version to keep (see section 2).

        3. Everyday saving and syncing

        Reading the footer

        Footer saysMeaningWhat to do
        inventory.json · saved today at 3:40 PM · auto-save onEverything is saved to the file.Nothing.
        inventory.json · unsaved changes · Save nowChanges are in the browser but not in the file yet.Click Save now.
        inventory.json · Reconnect to keep savingThe browser was restarted and wants your OK again.Click Reconnect, then Allow.
        Not using an inventory file yetItems are only in this browser.Set one up (section 1).

        After restarting Chrome or Edge

        For your security, the browser asks again before a web page can change a file. Click Reconnect to keep saving in the footer and choose Allow (or Edit files). If the file was updated on another device in the meantime, the app loads the newer version automatically.

        When both devices have changes

        If inventory.json was changed on another device and this device has unsaved changes, the app asks which version to keep:

        • Use the file's version: loads the file and drops this device's unsaved changes.
        • Keep this device's version: saves this device's items over the file.

        If you're not sure, click Back up now first so you have a copy of this device's items.

        Moving, renaming or switching files

        If you move or rename inventory.json, use Open existing file to pick it again. Stop using this file unlinks it. Your items stay in the browser, and the file itself is not deleted.

        4. Adding and editing items

        • Click Add Item. Only the name is required. Fill in category, type, room, value, photo and notes as you like.
        • Spot in Room: say exactly where the item is inside the room, such as Hall closet, top shelf or Bin 3. As you type, the app suggests spots you've already used in that room. Cards show it as Garage › Shelf 2, search finds it, and the All Spots filter next to the room filter shows just the items in one spot (pick a room first to list only that room's spots). It also appears on labels, QR codes, the insurance report and Excel/CSV exports. To import spots, use a column named Spot.
        • Show more fields: serial number, purchase date, warranty and receipt sit in a section at the bottom of the item window. Click Show more fields to open it. It opens by itself when you edit an item that already has any of these filled in. While closed, it shows how many are filled.
        • Photo: click Upload Photo to pick a picture, or on a phone or tablet Take Photo to use the camera. You can also paste an image link (that kind needs internet to show). Photos are shrunk automatically.
        • Search (top bar, after Snap & Add and Add Item): jumps down to the search box and puts the cursor in it, so you can start typing right away.
        • All (top bar, after Search): shows every item again. It clears the search box, every filter and any tag you picked, and scrolls to the list.
        • Snap & Add (top bar): opens the camera on a phone or tablet, or a file picker on a computer. Take the picture and a new item opens with the photo already in it. Type a name and save, or fill in the rest later.
        • Purchase date and warranty (under Show more fields): cards show "Bought …" and the warranty status. It turns amber when the warranty ends within 60 days.
        • Reminders appear at the top of the page when a warranty ends within 60 days (or ended in the last 30), and when you haven't backed up for over a week. Tap an item name to open it. Got it hides the warranty reminder until another warranty comes due; Remind me tomorrow snoozes the backup reminder. If your inventory file in OneDrive saves automatically, that counts as a backup.
        • Documents: set an item's Type to Document for things like passports, deeds, titles, insurance policies, wills or manuals. The item window then asks for a document number, date issued, expiry date and a document file (a scan, photo or PDF up to 5 MB; scans keep more detail so they stay readable). Cards show a file row with an Open button instead of a price, and the item view has Open document and Download. Documents that expire within 90 days show up in the reminders at the top.
        • Dashboard panels: tap a panel's title bar (Summary, Room, Type or Category) or its arrow to fold it up to one line, and tap again to open it. Collapse all and Expand all above the dashboard do every panel at once. Folded panels still show a short summary, and the app remembers your choice on this device.
        • Put in use on / Taken out of use on (under Show more fields): dates for personal property tax. Leave "Taken out of use on" empty while you still use the item. Both dates show in the item view and in Excel and CSV exports, and Excel or CSV imports read columns with these names (or "Placed in service" and "Retired").
        • Version log: tap the version number at the bottom of the screen (What's new) to see what each update added, newest first.
        • Reports menu: printable reports come first (Insurance Report, Items by Location, Personal Property Tax, Item Maintenance, Vehicle Maintenance, Police Report, All Items), then quick lists that filter the item list (Favorite Items, Items Marked to Move), then Moving and labels (Packing List, Print Labels), then downloads (Valuation Summary).
        • Tags: add any words you like to an item (for example gift, antique, kids or holiday). Type a tag and press Enter (or a comma); tap a suggestion to reuse a tag you already have; tap the × on a tag to remove it. Tags show as green chips on cards, in the list view and in the item view. Tap any tag chip to see every item with that tag. Your tags also appear as a row of chips under the search box: tap one to show only those items, and tap it again to show everything. You can also pick a tag in the All Tags box next to the other filters, search for a tag in the search box, and filter reports by Tag. Excel and CSV exports have a Tags column (tags separated by semicolons), and imports read it back.
        • Item maintenance (filters, checks and upkeep for things in your home; vehicles have their own service log instead, see Vehicles): under Show more fields, fill in what needs doing (for example Replace furnace filter), the Next due date and how often it Repeats. Items due within 30 days or overdue get an orange or red badge, and a reminder card appears on the main screen two weeks ahead. When you've done it, open the item and tap Mark done: a repeating task moves to its next date automatically. Reports › Maintenance Due prints a checklist sorted by due date (overdue, next 30 or 90 days, or everything), and Show › Item maintenance due soon or overdue works in every report's Filter box (vehicles have their own Vehicle service due filter).
        • Parts & filters: in the same Item maintenance box, tap Add a part or filter for each part the item takes: its name, part or model number, size, how many you have on hand, cost, where to buy it (a store or a web link) and notes. They show in the item view, on the Item Maintenance report next to the task, and in the Excel/CSV export (Maintenance Parts column). Vehicles have the same list in their Vehicle details box when you edit them (oil filter, air filter, wipers, tires); it shows in the vehicle's details and on the Vehicle Maintenance report.
        • Vehicles: set an item's Type to Vehicle and a Vehicle details box appears in the item window: make and model, year, current mileage, license plate and VIN. The Photo button next to Plate and next to VIN opens the camera (or a file picker on a computer) so you can photograph the plate or the VIN on the dashboard; the photo is saved with the vehicle. The app doesn't read the numbers from the photo by itself, so tap the photo to zoom in and type the number. Search finds a vehicle by its plate or VIN.
        • Vehicle service: open a vehicle to see its Service reminders and Service history. Add reminder sets something like Oil change every 5,000 miles or 6 months; it's due at whichever comes first, counted from when it was last done. Common services are one tap away and fill in typical intervals. Log service records the date, mileage, work done, cost, shop and a receipt (photo or PDF); tick the reminders it covers and they restart from that date and mileage. Update mileage keeps the mileage reminders accurate. A vehicle gets an orange or red badge when a service is within 500 miles or 30 days, or overdue, and a reminder card appears on the main screen.
        • Missing or stolen: open an item, tap Edit, and tap Report missing or stolen at the very bottom of the edit window (it is saved right away). Choose Missing or Stolen, the date you noticed, the police case number (if you've reported it) and what happened. The item gets a red Stolen or yellow Missing badge. When it turns up, open it and tap Mark as found. Reports › Missing or Stolen Items lists them on the main screen, and Show › Missing or stolen works in every report's Filter box.
        • Reports › Missing & stolen: this section of the Reports menu appears only while something is marked missing or stolen. Tap its title to fold it open or shut. It has Missing Items (shown when something is missing), Stolen Items (when something is stolen), Missing & Stolen (both) (when there are some of each), and the Police Report (when something is stolen). The first three are printable lists; the Police Report adds blanks for the police department, case number and your signature.
        • Police Report: a printable list of every missing or stolen item with its photo, make and model, serial number, value, purchase date, where it was kept, the date discovered, the case number and what happened, plus blanks for the police department, officer and claim number. Print it or save it as a PDF for the police or your insurer. The new Make / Model field (under Show more fields) helps here.
        • Deleting: tap the trash can on a card, in the item view, or Delete item at the bottom of the edit window. The app asks you to confirm, then shows Undo for a few seconds in case you change your mind.
        • Viewing an item: tap or click anywhere on an item card to see all its details in a clean, read-only view: big photo, value, where it is, serial, dates, warranty, receipt and notes. Tap Edit at the top to change it; when you save or cancel you return to the view. The view also has buttons to print its label and share it. Scanning a label opens this view too.
        • Type icons: every type gets a playful little icon, such as a car for Vehicle, toilet paper for Consumable, a scroll for Document, a toolbox for Equipment and a gem for Asset. Types you make up get one too when the name suggests it (for example Books, Toys, Jewelry, Garden or Wine), otherwise a tag. The icons show on cards, in the list and lines views, in the item view, on the Type filter bar and in the type menus, and they wiggle when you point at them.
        • Where am I? Each window, menu and report shows its name in small gray letters at the very top, such as Item details, Item editor, Reports or Insurance report.
        • Save and Cancel are at the top of the edit window, so you don't have to scroll down to save.
        • Duplicate check: when you add an item with the same name, or the same SKU/serial, as one you already have, the app tells you before saving. Choose Open that one, or Save anyway if you really have two.
        • Receipt (under Show more fields): attach a photo or a PDF up to 1 MB. Click Receipt on a card to view it. Receipts and documents open in a viewer inside the app; pinch to zoom on a phone, and use Download to save the file. Some phones can't show a PDF inside the app; then Download it and open it from Files.
        • Favorite (star) and Move (moving list) can be toggled on each card.
        • Phones and tablets: the app notices a touch screen and makes the buttons on each item larger and easier to tap, in their own row, with larger item names and locations. It also uses larger text in forms, so the iPhone doesn't zoom in while you type.
        • Edit lists: categories, rooms and types are your own lists. Click Edit next to a field or Settings › Manage Lists to add, rename or delete options. Renaming updates every item that uses it. Order this list shows each list as added, A to Z, or with the most-used first, and the dropdowns follow the same order.
        • Use the pencil to edit and the trash can to delete an item.

        5. Finding items and the dashboard

        • Search by name, room, serial number, make and model, tag, plate or VIN. Results update as you type; tap Go (or Search on the phone keyboard) to close the keyboard and jump to the results.
        • Under the search box is one line with Sort, Filter and View. Sort picks the order or grouping. Filter opens the category, room, spot, type and tag boxes; the number on it shows how many filters are on. View switches between Cards, a compact List, and Lines (one line per item: name, room, value). Searching with nothing typed shows all items. When the list is grouped (by type, room or category), tap a section heading such as Asset, Vehicle or Document to fold it closed or open it again; Collapse all and Expand all do every section at once. Clear filters appears while a filter is on. Inside the filter boxes, Clear all filters sets them all back to All but keeps your search. Under the search box, Clear tag turns off the tag you tapped. On an item, Clear all tags removes its tags. In Manage Lists › Tags, Clear all tags removes every tag from every item.
        • Click any dashboard card (a category, room or type) to show just those items.
        • Switch between Grid and List view. The sort menu next to the filters sorts A to Z (or Z to A), by date added, by purchase date or by value, or groups items under headings by category, room or type, with a count and total for each group. The app remembers your choice, and it also applies to the moving and favorites lists and to Excel and CSV exports.
        • Settings menu (gear icon, formerly View; close it with the × at the top or the Close button at the bottom). Manage Lists is here too (and in the Data menu): add, rename, delete and order categories, rooms and types, and on the Tags tab rename a tag on every item at once, delete a tag from every item, or add tags ahead of time so they're suggested when you tag items: hide or show the dashboard, choose which panels appear, pick an accent color, and choose Light / Dark. Device (the default) follows your phone or computer's light or dark setting and changes with it; if the device doesn't say, it uses the time of day. Time is dark from 7 PM to 7 AM. Light and Dark stay fixed.

        6. Reports, insurance report and labels

        • Reports › Insurance Report (Print): totals by room and category, then every item with photo, purchase date, warranty, receipt status and value. Use Group by (room, category or type) and Sort (value, A to Z, date added or purchase date) at the top of the report. It has blank lines for your policy details and a signature. Then by adds subgroups inside each group (for example Room, then Category), each with its own count and total. Use Print / Save PDF, then keep a copy outside your home.
        • Reports › Personal Property Tax: a printable list for your property tax return. Mark items for it with the Add to tax report button at the very bottom of the edit window (tap Save to keep it). Pick the Tax year: an item is listed if it was put in use (or bought, if no in-use date) by the end of that year and not taken out of use before the year began. It shows purchase date, cost, the in-use dates and how much of the year each item was in use, grouped by category, room or type. Include › All items in use also lists items you haven't marked, and the Show › In tax report filter works in the other reports too.
        • Reports › All Items (one line each): a compact list with one line per item: name, room › spot, category, type and value. Choose Group by (room, room › spot, category or type), a sort order, Columns › Add SKU and purchase date, and whether to show values. It uses the same Filter row as the other reports, and tapping a line opens that item.
        • Reports › Items by Location: a printable list of everything room by room, grouped by Spot in Room (for example Garage › Shelf 2), with item counts and values for each room and spot. At the top you can pick one room, sort A to Z or by value, hide values, add small photos, and start each room on its own page. That's handy for a sheet to keep in each room or for packing.
        • Reports › Vehicle Maintenance: for each vehicle, its plate, VIN and mileage, the upcoming service (what's due, at what mileage or date, and how close it is) and the service history with dates, mileage, work done, shop, cost and a total. Pick one vehicle or all, and how much history to show (all, the last 12 months, this year, or upcoming only). Print it or save it as a PDF for a sale or warranty claim.
        • Items Marked to Move and Favorite Items Report filter the list.
        • Valuation Summary downloads a CSV with totals.

        Printing labels with QR codes

        Open Reports › Print Labels (QR), or open an item and click Print label.

        1. Which items: all items, the items shown in the list right now (after a search or filter), one category, one room, one type, items marked to move, or favorites. Untick any item you don't want, or click None and tick just the ones you want.
        2. Label type:
          • DYMO 30334 (2-1/4 × 1-1/4 in) for DYMO LabelWriter printers. Each label prints as its own page.
          • Avery 5160 (1 × 2-5/8 in, 30 per letter sheet) for any regular printer. The same layout fits Avery 5260, 5960, 8160 and 18160. Use Skip the first to start on a partly used sheet.
        3. Choose what to show (QR code, room and category, SKU or serial, value) and how many copies of each.
        4. Click Preview labels, check them, then click Print labels.

        Report filters and sorting

        • The Insurance Report and Items by Location have a Filter row at the top: Room, Spot (after you pick a room), Category, Type, Show (favorites, marked to move, packed, under warranty, missing a photo, missing a receipt) and Contains (a word in the name, notes, serial, spot or box).
        • All totals on the report follow the filters, and the printed report says what it's limited to. Clear filters goes back to everything. Both reports share the same filters, and the app remembers them for next time.
        • Sort works on every report: value (high or low first), name (A to Z or Z to A), purchase date or date added (newest or oldest first).
        • Group by and then by (Insurance Report) or Split rooms by (Items by Location) choose the main groups and subgroups: Room, Room › Spot, Category or Type.
        • Hide settings at the top of a report folds away the group, sort and filter controls so you see more of the report. Show settings brings them back; while hidden, it says how many filters are on. The app remembers your choice.
        • Tap any item in a report (including the packing box list) to open its details on top of the report. Close it to return to the same spot in the report; if you edited the item, the report updates.
        • Tip: "Missing a photo" or "Missing a receipt" makes a quick to-do list before you send the report to your insurer.

        Packing list (for a move)

        • Open Reports › Packing List. It lists the items marked to Move; tap All items to pack everything.
        • Type a box name under Packing into box (for example Box 1 or Kitchen 3). Tap the big check box next to an item when it's packed and it goes into that box. Next box moves on to Box 2, Box 3 and so on.
        • You can also type a box next to any item, or change it later.
        • Scan to pack: scan each item's label as it goes in the box. It's checked off and put in the current box, and the camera stays on for the next one.
        • Use To pack / Packed to see what's left, and By box to see what's in each box. The bar at the top shows your progress.
        • Print box lists prints what's in each box. Tick Each box on its own page to tape a list to each box.
        • Uncheck all (tap twice) starts over and keeps the box names. Packed items and boxes are saved with your inventory and in your inventory file.

        Scanning a label

        • Tap Scan at the top and point the camera at a label's QR code. The item opens as soon as the code is read, so you can check or change it.
        • Where the live camera isn't allowed (some browsers and previews), tap Take a photo of the label. Fill most of the picture with the label, in good light.
        • If the label belongs to another inventory on this device, the app offers to switch to it and opens the item there.
        • Your phone's own camera app can also read a label. It shows the item's details as text but doesn't open the app.
        PrinterIn the print window
        DYMO LabelWriterDestination: your DYMO LabelWriter. Paper size: 30334 (may be listed as 30334 Medium or 2-1/4 in × 1-1/4 in). Margins: None. Scale: 100%. Turn off headers and footers. If the label comes out sideways, switch the layout to Landscape.
        Avery sheetPaper: Letter. Margins: None. Scale: 100% (not "Fit to page"). Print one test sheet on plain paper and hold it against a label sheet first.

        The QR code holds plain text: the item name, room, category, SKU or serial and the item's ID. Scan it with any phone camera to see what is in a box or which item it is, even without internet. The code isn't a web link, so scanning it doesn't open the app.

        Printing doesn't work inside a preview window. Open the downloaded .html file in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox to print.

        7. Backups, Excel, CSV and where files are saved

        • Settings › Try the Sample Home opens a separate inventory called Sample Home with about two dozen example items: appliances, electronics, furniture, tools, valuables, documents, a car with service history, household supplies, and one missing and one stolen item. Use it to try the reports, labels and filters without touching your own items. Switch back from the inventory menu at the top; delete it there when you're done.
        • Settings › Import templates downloads a sample Excel or CSV file with every column the app understands and a few example items (a TV, a sofa, a car, a document and a tool). Replace the sample rows with your own, keep the headings, and bring it in with Data › Import Data. Only the Name column is required; leave the Item ID column blank for new items.
        • Scan also reads product barcodes (UPC, EAN, Code 128 and others) from a photo. If an item already has that number in its SKU / Serial, it opens. If not, tap Add item with this barcode; inside the Claude app, Add with AI details also suggests the name, make and model, category and a typical price from the photo. Check the suggestions before saving.
        • Data › Household Sync keeps one shared copy of the inventory online, so all your devices and the people you share the app with see the same items, photos and receipts. On the app's claude.ai page, tap Share and invite family by email as an Editor; they open the link and tap Join the shared inventory. Each device keeps its own full copy too, so the app still works offline.
        • Data › Combine Files reads several saved files at once (JSON backups, inventory.json, Excel or CSV), joins them with the items already in the app and keeps one copy of each item. It shows the totals first; nothing changes until you tap Combine, and Undo puts things back.
        • How to use this app: Help & User Manual (link in the footer, under the app name) opens this manual. The Help button at the top of the page opens it too.
        • Suggest a Feature or Report a Problem (footer, and in the menu) opens a short form. Pick idea or problem, write a few words and tap Send; the app version and device type go with it. If Send isn't available (for example in a downloaded copy of the app), use Gmail, Email app or Copy message to send it to tomdaube@gmail.com. The app's owner sees everything sent at the bottom of the same form.
        • Menu (the ☰ button at the top left, beside the app name) lists everything the app can do in one place, grouped into Items, Reports, Moving and labels, Data and files, Organize, and Share and help. Type in Find a function to narrow the list.
        • Back up now (footer) or Data › Export JSON saves a complete backup, including photos and receipts. The footer shows your last backup date. It turns amber after 7 days.
        • Settings › Export all items › Excel spreadsheet (also in the Data menu) creates a real .xlsx file with dollar values, dates, filters and a total row. CSV file is the same data as plain text.
        • Data › Import Data restores a JSON backup or inventory.json (this replaces the current items). It also adds items from an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file. The app reads the first sheet; it needs a header row with at least a Name column (Category, Room, Type, Value, SKU, Purchase Date, Warranty Expires, Notes and Item ID are also recognized). Rows with a matching Item ID are updated, so you can export to Excel, edit there and import the file back. Old .xls files need to be saved as .xlsx first.

        Choosing where files are saved

        Every file the app makes (backups, Excel and CSV exports, reports, and copies of the app itself) lets you pick the folder and name when your browser allows it:

        • Chrome or Edge on a computer: a Save As window opens. Pick any folder, such as OneDrive or Documents, and change the name if you like. The next save starts in the same folder.
        • iPhone, iPad and Android: the share menu opens. Choose Save to Files (or OneDrive), then the folder.
        • Safari or Firefox on a computer: files go to Downloads unless you tell the browser to ask:
          • Safari: Safari › Settings › General › File download location › Ask for each download.
          • Firefox: Settings › General › Files and Applications, then turn on Always ask you where to save files.
          • Chrome or Edge (if the Save As window ever doesn't appear): Settings › Downloads › Ask where to save each file before downloading.
        An inventory.json in OneDrive is already a cloud backup. An occasional Back up now file saved somewhere else is still a good idea.

        8. Sharing the app

        Click Share the App (at the bottom of the page, or in the Settings menu), enter one or more email addresses and an optional note, then click Email App. The app asks where to save a blank copy (Home_Inventory_App.html), then opens a ready-made email. Attach the file from that folder and press Send. Your own items are never included. On phones, Share File… opens the share menu with the file attached.

        More than one inventory

        Keep separate inventories, for example Tom's Stuff, Linda's Gear or Lake House. Each has its own items, photos, rooms and categories, inventory file and backups. Click the inventory name next to the title at the top:

        • Switch by picking a name from the list.
        • New inventory… starts an empty one.
        • Save this inventory to a file saves a complete copy, photos included (the same as Back up now). The file name starts with the inventory's name.
        • Open inventory from a file… opens a saved file as a new inventory, for example a file Linda sent you or one from another device. The inventory you are in isn't changed. To replace the current inventory with a file instead, use Data › Import Data.
        • Rename and Delete work on the inventory you are in. Delete removes it from this browser only, not any files you saved.
        • The insurance report, labels and exports use the inventory you are in. Each inventory can link to its own inventory file (Data › Inventory File), such as Toms_Stuff.json in OneDrive.

        9. Storage limits and troubleshooting

        • Storage: item details use the browser's small storage area (about 5 MB, enough for thousands of items). Photos and receipts go in its large photo storage, which can hold hundreds of MB, so thousands of photos. This works in Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox, and on iPhone, iPad and Android. The footer shows how much each part uses. Photos from older versions move over automatically the first time you open v2.24.
        • Photos are kept per browser. Each device and browser has its own copy. Your backups and inventory.json contain every photo, so open the file on another device to bring them along.
        • iPhone and iPad: Safari may clear a website's data after a few weeks unused. Add the app to your Home Screen (Share › Add to Home Screen), which keeps it, and use Back up now regularly.
        • "Could not save to inventory.json": check that OneDrive is running and signed in, and that the file wasn't moved. Use Open existing file to pick it again.
        • The app shows plain text with no icons or colors: versions before v2.20 downloaded their look and icons from the internet each time they opened, so they looked broken offline or inside a file preview (OneDrive, the Files app, an email or chat preview). From v2.20 everything is built into the file. If you still see plain text, you are probably opening an older copy.
        • Files always land in Downloads: see Choosing where files are saved in section 6.
        • No Create or Open window appears: make sure you opened the downloaded .html file directly, not a preview inside another app.
        • Items look different on two devices: the device that saved last wins. Open the file again with Open existing file to load the latest version.
        • Delete doesn't ask for confirmation or do anything: some previews block pop-ups. Open the .html file directly in your browser.
